meta.trial_name: REDUCE-IT (Reduction of Cardiovascular Events with Icosapent Ethyl-Intervention Trial)
meta.drug: icosapent ethyl (AMR101, Vascepa), 2 g twice daily (4 g/day)
meta.mechanism: highly purified eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) ethyl ester; lowers triglycerides ~20% placebo-adjusted with small apoB/non-HDL-C effects. No single protein target: ChEMBL lists the mechanism as unknown; the label lists increased beta-oxidation, DGAT inhibition, decreased hepatic lipogenesis and increased plasma lipoprotein lipase activity as potential mechanisms and says CV-event mechanisms are 'not completely understood but are likely multi-factorial'. target_symbol LPL is used as the triglyceride-pathway proxy (the pathway tested by Ference 2019 LPL Mendelian randomization), not as a proven drug target.
meta.modality: oral small molecule / purified omega-3 fatty acid ethyl ester (capsules)
meta.indication: reduction of ischemic events in statin-treated patients with established cardiovascular disease or diabetes plus risk factors, with fasting triglycerides 135/150-499 mg/dL and LDL-C 41-100 mg/dL

n_randomized.quote: A total of 8179 patients were enrolled (70.7% for secondary prevention of cardiovascular events) and were followed for a median of 4.9 years.
n_randomized.note: 4089 icosapent ethyl, 4090 placebo (Fig. 4 column headers; registry S3).

median_followup.quote: The median duration of follow-up was 4.9 years (maximum, 6.2 years).
median_followup.note: Press release S2 also: 'Median follow-up time in REDUCE-IT was 4.9 years.'

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, or unstable angina (5-point MACE); key secondary: CV death, nonfatal MI or nonfatal stroke
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, or unstable angina. The key secondary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.
primary_endpoint.note: Registry S3 primary outcome wording: unstable angina 'determined to be caused by myocardial ischemia by invasive / non-invasive testing and requiring emergent hospitalization'; MI includes silent MI.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=45 with established CVD or >=50 with diabetes plus >=1 risk factor; stable statin >=4 weeks; fasting TG 150-499 mg/dL (10% variability allowance gave an effective lower limit of 135 mg/dL; later amended to >=200 mg/dL); LDL-C 41-100 mg/dL
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: who had been receiving statin therapy and who had a fasting triglyceride level of 135 to 499 mg per deciliter (1.52 to 5.63 mmol per liter) and a low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level of 41 to 100 mg per deciliter (1.06 to 2.59 mmol per liter).
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Methods: 'Eligible patients had a fasting triglyceride level of 150 to 499 mg per deciliter'; the initial protocol allowed a 10% lower level; Discussion: required level 'subsequently changed to >=200 mg per deciliter'; 10.3% of enrolled patients had TG <150 mg/dL at baseline. Age criteria from design paper S4 abstract.

planned_events.quote: approximately 1612 adjudicated primary end-point events would be necessary to provide the trial with 90% power to detect a 15% lower risk of the primary composite end point in the icosapent ethyl group than in the placebo group.
planned_events.note: Also in design paper S4 (2017-03-15): 'The sample-size calculation was based on a hazard ratio assumption of 0.85. Therefore, 1612 events would be required to have approximately 90% power with a 1-sided alpha-level of 2.5% and with 2 interim analyses.' Target sample size 7990.

assumed_rrr.quote: 90% power to detect a 15% lower risk of the primary composite end point
assumed_rrr.note: Design paper S4: 'hazard ratio assumption of 0.85'.

power.quote: would be necessary to provide the trial with 90% power

alpha.unit: two-sided (final analysis, after two interim analyses)
alpha.quote: If the risk of the primary composite end point was significantly lower with icosapent ethyl than with placebo at a final two-sided alpha level of 0.0437 (as determined with the use of O'Brien-Fleming boundaries generated with the Lan-DeMets alphaspending function approach after accounting for two prespecified interim efficacy analyses)
alpha.note: Overall design alpha: 1-sided 2.5% (= two-sided 0.05) per design paper S4; registry S3: 'The 2-sided alpha level for the primary analysis was adjusted to 0.0437 from 0.05 to account for the two interim analyses'.

stopped_early.quote: In this event-driven trial, it was estimated that approximately 1612 adjudicated primary end-point events would be necessary
stopped_early.note: Ran to completion; 1606 primary events observed (705 + 901). Not stopped at either interim analysis.

baseline.quote: At baseline, the median LDL cholesterol level was 75.0 mg per deciliter (1.94 mmol per liter)
baseline.note: 1.94 mmol/L. Derived LDL-C (preparative ultracentrifugation preferred, then direct, Friedewald, Hopkins; Table 1 footnote). Baseline LDL-C differed slightly between groups (P=0.03): FDA S6 Table 24 derived LDL-C 74 vs 76 mg/dL.

baseline.quote: and the median triglyceride level was 216.0 mg per deciliter (2.44 mmol per liter).
the median high-density lipoprotein cholesterol level was 40.0 mg per deciliter (1.03 mmol per liter)

baseline.note: Quote = verbatim cells of the Non-HDL-C rows (baseline, year 1, change, % change); the row label sits on a separate line in the PDF layout. FDA reviewer's summary of sponsor data. ~3.05 mmol/L.
Quote = verbatim cells of the Apo-B rows (baseline, year 2, change, % change); row label on a separate line in the PDF layout.
Quote = verbatim cells of the hs-CRP rows (baseline, year 2, change, % change). ACC summary also gives baseline hs-CRP 2.2.

biomarker_effects.method: fasting central lab; median change, between-group difference by Hodges-Lehmann estimate
biomarker_effects.quote: the median reduction from baseline (as estimated with the use of the Hodges-Lehmann approach) was 19.7% greater in the icosapent ethyl group than in the placebo group (a 44.5 mg per deciliter [0.50 mmol per liter] greater reduction; P<0.001).
biomarker_effects.note: Within-arm: -18.3% (-39.0 mg/dL) icosapent ethyl vs +2.2% (+4.5 mg/dL) placebo. Absolute = -0.50 mmol/L.

biomarker_effects.quote: The median change in LDL cholesterol level from baseline was an increase of 3.1% (2.0 mg per deciliter [0.05 mmol per liter]) in the icosapent ethyl group and an increase of 10.2% (7.0 mg per deciliter [0.18 mmol per liter]) in the placebo group — a 6.6% (5.0 mg per deciliter [0.13 mmol per liter]) lower increase with icosapent ethyl than with placebo (P<0.001).
biomarker_effects.note: The 'reduction' is mostly a rise in the mineral-oil placebo arm (+10.2%), not a fall on drug. Hopkins LDL-C (FDA S6 Table 24): -1.2% vs +10.9%; Friedewald +3.5% vs +12.9%; ultracentrifugation +2.8% vs +10.0%. -5.0 mg/dL.

biomarker_effects.method: calculated (TC minus HDL-C); between-group difference as used by Marston meta-regression
biomarker_effects.quote: The observed clinical benefit of 25% relative risk reduction was well beyond the approximately 9% risk reduction expected based on the 0.41 mmol/L of non-HDL-C lowering
biomarker_effects.note: Consistent with FDA S6 Table 24 within-arm medians: icosapent ethyl -4 mg/dL (-3.6%) vs placebo +12 mg/dL (+10.4%), difference 16 mg/dL = 0.41 mmol/L (derived). Kastelein & Stroes editorial S5 cites 'median reduction of 14 mg per deciliter (0.36 mmol per liter) in non-HDL cholesterol level from baseline' (likely the Hodges-Lehmann estimate from NEJM Table S4, not read). Percent difference by Hodges-Lehmann NOT FOUND (Table S4 not accessed); difference of median % changes = -14.0 points (derived).

biomarker_effects.method: central lab immunoassay; within-arm median changes
biomarker_effects.location: FDA briefing document, Table 24 (footnote: Apo B and hsCRP were measured at Year 2)
biomarker_effects.note: DERIVED placebo adjustment: difference of within-arm medians (-2.5% minus +7.8% = -10.3 points; -2 minus +6 = -8 mg/dL), not a Hodges-Lehmann estimate. Editorial S5: apoB rose 7.8% at 2 years in the placebo group. NEJM Table S4 Hodges-Lehmann value not accessed.

biomarker_effects.method: hs-CRP measured at baseline and day 720 only
biomarker_effects.quote: The estimated hazard ratio per unit hs-CRP value suggests that the approximately 0.65 mg/L (50%) difference in hs-CRP between arms from baseline would increase the risk of cardiovascular outcomes by less than 0.3% in the placebo arm of the REDUCE-IT trial.
biomarker_effects.location: FDA briefing document, Clinical Pharmacology, effect of hs-CRP
biomarker_effects.note: Within-arm (Table 24): -13.9% icosapent ethyl vs +32.3% placebo. Marston S7 cites 'a between-group difference at 2 years of 0.9 mg/L'. Ridker S9 (2022 substudy) between-group median % difference at end of study 38.5% for hsCRP. Most of the difference is a rise on mineral oil.

biomarker_effects.quote: AMR101 4 and 2 g/day significantly decreased TG levels by 21.5% (p <0.0001) and 10.1% (p = 0.0005), respectively, and non-high-density lipoprotein (non-HDL) cholesterol by 13.6% (p <0.0001) and 5.5% (p = 0.0054), respectively.
biomarker_effects.note: ANCHOR (n=702; statin-treated, TG 200-<500, LDL-C 40-<100 mg/dL), same mineral-oil placebo; published 2012-07-20, before readout. Abstract read only.

biomarker_effects.quote: AMR101 4 g/day decreased LDL cholesterol by 6.2% (p = 0.0067) and decreased apolipoprotein B (9.3%), total cholesterol (12.0%), very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (24.4%), lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A(2) (19.0%), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (22.0%) versus placebo (p <0.001 for all comparisons).
biomarker_effects.note: Same sentence gives LDL-C -6.2% and hsCRP -22.0% vs placebo. FDA S6: the ANCHOR placebo arm also showed an LDL-C rise (8.8% by ultracentrifugation), so these placebo-adjusted values partly reflect the comparator. Before readout.

biomarker_effects.method: Hodges-Lehmann median of [drug % change - placebo % change]
biomarker_effects.note: MARINE: only ~25% on statins; no LDL-C rise on placebo (FDA S6: '-3% change from baseline'). Label Table 2 also: apoB -9 (-14, -3), non-HDL-C -18 (-25, -11), LDL-C -2 (-13, +8). MARINE published 2011 (before readout); values here read from the current label.

hr.quote: A primary end-point event occurred in 17.2% of the patients in the icosapent ethyl group, as compared with 22.0% of the patients in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68 to 0.83; P<0.001)
hr.note: Key secondary 11.2% vs 14.8%, HR 0.74 (0.65-0.83); CV death 4.3% vs 5.2%, HR 0.80 (0.66-0.98), P=0.03; death from any cause 274 (6.7%) vs 310 (7.6%), HR 0.87 (0.74-1.02) (Fig. 4). Registry S3: HR 0.75 (0.68-0.83), p=0.00000001. Topline S2: 'approximately 25% relative risk reduction ... (p<0.001)'.

p.quote: hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68 to 0.83; P<0.001
p.note: Registry S3 log-rank p = 0.00000001 vs final alpha 0.0437.

events_control.note: Registry S3 primary outcome count 901. Total 1606 vs 1612 planned.

safety_signals.value: Hospitalization for atrial fibrillation or flutter higher: 3.1% vs 2.1%, P=0.004
safety_signals.quote: A larger percentage of patients in the icosapent ethyl group than in the placebo group were hospitalized for atrial fibrillation or flutter (3.1% vs. 2.1%, P=0.004).
safety_signals.note: Label S13: 127 (3%) vs 84 (2%); now a Warning and Precaution. FDA S6: greater in patients with prior AF/flutter.

safety_signals.value: Serious bleeding 2.7% vs 2.1% (P=0.06); no fatal bleeding; any bleeding 12% vs 10%
safety_signals.quote: Serious bleeding events occurred in 2.7% of the patients in the icosapent ethyl group and in 2.1% in the placebo group (P=0.06).
safety_signals.note: Label S13: '482 (12%) patients receiving VASCEPA experienced a bleeding event compared to 404 (10%) patients receiving placebo'. Hemorrhagic stroke 0.3% vs 0.2% (P=0.55).

safety_signals.value: Mineral-oil placebo arm showed rises in LDL-C (~10%), non-HDL-C, apoB and hsCRP (+32%), raising concern that the comparator was not inert (possible reduced statin absorption)
safety_signals.quote: While REDUCE-IT demonstrated a significant benefit on CV outcomes, the pattern of lipid and inflammatory biomarkers measured during the course of the trial raises questions about the internal validity of the study.
safety_signals.note: Comparator issue rather than a drug toxicity; listed here because it bears on internal validity. FDA: worst-case LDL-C effect would raise placebo risk by ~3%; 'could not account for the positive CV outcomes'.

genetics.finding: Triglyceride-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants give the same CHD protection per 10 mg/dL lower apoB; TG and LDL-C associations become null after adjusting for apoB, so the benefit of TG lowering should be proportional to the absolute apoB change
genetics.effect: OR 0.771 (0.741-0.802) per 10 mg/dL lower apoB (LPL score); TG OR 1.014 (0.965-1.065) after apoB adjustment
genetics.quote: Triglyceride-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants were associated with similar lower risk of CHD per unit difference in ApoB. Therefore, the clinical benefit of lowering triglyceride and LDL-C levels may be proportional to the absolute change in ApoB.
genetics.note: After readout. Discussion (PMC full text): 'the reported reductions in cardiovascular events in the JELIS and REDUCE-IT trials were far greater than what would have been expected from the modest observed changes in plasma lipid levels, thus suggesting that the observed clinical benefit of the omega-3 fatty acid eicosapentaenoic acid may be largely due to its non-lipid-related effects.'

genetics.finding: Rare APOC3 loss-of-function mutations: 39% lower triglycerides and 40% lower CHD risk (triglyceride-rich lipoprotein pathway is causal)
genetics.quote: The risk of coronary heart disease among 498 carriers of any rare APOC3 mutation was 40% lower than the risk among 110,472 noncarriers (odds ratio, 0.60; 95% confidence interval, 0.47 to 0.75; P=4×10(-6)).
genetics.note: Before readout. Supports the TG-rich lipoprotein pathway, but genetic effects are lifelong and carriers also have lower apoB-containing lipoproteins; says nothing about EPA specifically.

genetics.finding: No human genetic evidence for a specific EPA drug target; mechanism of the CV benefit unknown
genetics.quote: Mechanisms responsible for the benefit of icosapent ethyl observed in REDUCE-IT are currently not known.
genetics.note: Trial authors' statement (Discussion). ChEMBL records the icosapent ethyl mechanism as 'Unknown'.

consensus_explanation.summary: REDUCE-IT clearly met its primary endpoint (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.68-0.83, 1606 events) with consistent secondary endpoints including CV death (HR 0.80), and the FDA approved a CV-risk-reduction indication. Experts agreed, however, that the benefit is far larger than the lipid change predicts: the editorialists (Kastelein & Stroes) estimated that the non-HDL-C change would give only a 6-8% lower risk and that the hsCRP change would add about 5%, Marston et al. called REDUCE-IT the most striking outlier in the TG meta-regression (25% observed vs ~9% expected from 0.41 mmol/L non-HDL-C lowering), and Ference et al. concluded that the benefit of EPA may be largely due to non-lipid effects. Benefit was similar across baseline and achieved TG levels, so TG lowering per se is not the accepted explanation; the mechanism remains unknown. The second caveat is the mineral-oil placebo: LDL-C rose ~10%, apoB ~8% and hsCRP ~32% in the placebo arm (also IL-6, IL-1beta and Lp-PLA2 per Ridker 2022), possibly by reducing statin absorption. The FDA judged that the worst-case LDL-C effect (~3% higher risk) could not account for the result, but Doi/Nordestgaard estimated that lipid/CRP changes explain only an HR of 0.88, leaving an unexplained 13% attributable to other effects of EPA or of mineral oil, and the corn-oil-controlled STRENGTH trial of EPA+DHA was neutral (HR 0.99). Safety caveats were more atrial fibrillation hospitalizations (3.1% vs 2.1%) and a trend to more serious bleeding.

pre_readout.note: readout_date 2018-09-24 (Amarin topline press release: ~25% RRR, p<0.001, no HR/CI or lipid data). HR, events and lipid changes first public 2018-11-10 (AHA/NEJM).
available_before_readout: Registry record with endpoints and eligibility (S3, first posted 2011-12-15)
JELIS open-label EPA 1.8 g/day trial: 19% lower major coronary events (S15, 2007-03-31)
ANCHOR 12-week lipid effects of 4 g/day in a REDUCE-IT-like population vs the same mineral-oil placebo: TG -21.5%, non-HDL-C -13.6%, apoB -9.3%, LDL-C -6.2%, hsCRP -22.0% (S12, 2012-07-20)
MARINE lipid effects in TG >=500 mg/dL (2011; read here from label S13)
Design: 1612 events, 90% power for HR 0.85, 1-sided alpha 2.5% with 2 interims, ~8000 patients (design paper S4, 2017-03-15)
APOC3 loss-of-function genetics: TG-rich lipoprotein pathway causal for CHD (S14, 2014-06-18)

Mineral-oil placebo concern: the ANCHOR placebo arm showed rising LDL-C (FDA S6 cites 8.8% by ultracentrifugation) and the October 2013 FDA advisory committee on ANCHOR questioned whether mineral oil was inert (news reports only; the 2013 briefing document was not read)
only_after_readout: Phase 3 HR, CI, events and placebo-adjusted TG/LDL-C changes (S1, 2018-11-10)
Editorial estimate that lipid and CRP changes explain only ~6-8% + ~5% of risk reduction, and mineral-oil concern (S5, 2018-11-16)
LPL vs LDLR Mendelian randomization: benefit proportional to apoB (S8, 2019-01-29)
Marston meta-regression: REDUCE-IT the main outlier, ~9% expected vs 25% observed (S7, 2019-09-18)
FDA briefing analysis of the mineral-oil placebo, apoB and hsCRP at 2 years (S6, 2019-11-14)
Doi/Nordestgaard cohort mimicking: expected HR 0.88 from lipid/CRP changes (S10, 2021-08-29)
Ridker biomarker substudy: IL-6, IL-1beta, hsCRP, Lp-PLA2, OxLDL rise on mineral oil (S9, 2022-06-28)

open_questions: Hodges-Lehmann placebo-adjusted percent changes for apoB, non-HDL-C and hsCRP (NEJM Supplementary Table S4) were not accessed. apoB -10.3% / -8 mg/dL is a DERIVED difference of within-arm medians at year 2 (FDA S6 Table 24); non-HDL-C -0.41 mmol/L is from Marston S7 (consistent with FDA within-arm medians), while editorial S5 cites 0.36 mmol/L (14 mg/dL).

How much of the 25% RRR reflects harm from the mineral-oil comparator is unresolved: FDA S6 estimated ~3% from the LDL-C rise and judged it insufficient to explain the result; Doi/Nordestgaard S10 estimated an expected HR of 0.88 from lipid and CRP changes in both arms; Ridker S9 found multiple inflammatory markers rising on mineral oil and said only a new trial with a non-mineral-oil comparator could settle it.
Whether the EPA-only formulation or the dose explains the contrast with STRENGTH (EPA+DHA vs corn oil, HR 0.99) and other neutral omega-3 trials remains debated.
target_symbol LPL is a pathway proxy, not an established molecular target of EPA; ChEMBL lists the mechanism as unknown.
Eligibility: abstract says TG 135-499 mg/dL; methods say 150-499 with a 10% variability allowance; protocol later amended to >=200 mg/dL; press release says 150-499.
Alpha: final two-sided 0.0437 after two interim analyses (overall one-sided 0.025).
